alt: Core #2 of 60 cover: Parliament: sessions and business, asked 24 times in UPSC Prelims 2016 to 2026, with a bar chart by year. Aarav asks if he should memorise Parliament trivia; Priya says learn the rules: who, when, which House.
The pattern: 8 questions on bills, sessions and motions; 6 on the Speaker, members and posts; 3 on committees; 7 others. 19 of 24 are statement questions; 2024 alone set 6.
Three UPSC traps: facing removal, the Speaker may still speak and vote (2024); Article 102 never defines office of profit (2019); prorogation lapses no Bill, only Lok Sabha dissolution can (2016).
The latest three PYQs: 2026 Q59 SC/ST Welfare Committee, answer d (provisional); 2026 Q58 starred vs unstarred questions, answer c (provisional); 2025 Q88 defection and political party, answer d.

Read this first: NCERT Class 11 Indian Constitution at Work, chapter 5 Legislature and chapter 4 Executive; NCERT Class 12 Politics in India since Independence, chapter 2 Era of One-party Dominance. Skip who said what in which debate.

This sub-topic's row in the Syllabus X-Ray: five stars, 24 questions, 2.1 percent weight, with sources. One Core a week here, all 60 in the X-Ray today. 199 rupees till 30 November, then 249. A new Core every Thursday.
